jobs.title: Controller - Austria
jobs.description: About Tempo Based in San Diego, California, Tempo develops thermochemical energy storage (TCES) systems designed for energy-intensive industries. The platform enables industrial operators to shift energy use over time by sourcing power when it is most cost-effective and enables the electrification of high-temperature industrial heat at a cost advantage to using fossil fuels. By storing electricity thermochemically, the system delivers a continuous stream of combustion-free, high-temperature air at up to 1,200°C. Tempo is backed by leading climate and energy investors, including Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Khosla Ventures, and Prelude Ventures. For more information, visit www.tempoenergy.com . Role Summary Tempo is seeking a Senior Accountant / Finance Manager (m/w/d) to join its Austrian subsidiary, Tempo Energy Innovations GmbH, based in Dornbirn, Vorarlberg. This is a fully remote, permanent position, available full-time at 38.5 hours per week; a part-time arrangement from 30 hours per week is negotiable. The role reports to the Director of Finance & Accounting in the United States and is expected to begin as soon as possible. Both German and English are required as working languages. The Senior Accountant / Finance Manager will serve as the sole owner of the finance function for Tempo's Austrian entity, with end-to-end responsibility for accounting, payroll, tax, purchasing, and EU grant reporting. This is an individual contributor role, working in close coordination with the Director of Finance & Accounting in the United States and alongside Tempo's external Steuerberater and payroll provider. Responsibilities Accounting and Month-End Close Own AP, AR, GL, bank and credit card reconciliations, fixed assets and depreciation, accruals, prepaids, and inventory and WIP for prototype and pilot builds. Close monthly to the group calendar: reconcile all balance sheet accounts and deliver the close package on deadline. Maintain multi-currency accounting (EUR functional, USD group reporting), FX revaluation, and intercompany balances with the US parent and Spanish holding entity. Prepare the Jahresabschluss under UGB with our Steuerberater, plus the bridge to US GAAP for group consolidation. Deliver monthly management reporting by cost centre and project. Support the group audit: PBC schedules, sample support, documentation. Payroll Run the monthly Lohnverrechnung cycle with our external provider; review the payroll register and post payroll journals. Administer ÖGK and ELDA filings, Lohnsteuer, DB, DZ, and Kommunalsteuer. Maintain employee master data, leave accruals, expense reimbursements, Taggeld and Nächtigungsgeld. Allocate personnel cost by project, work package, and cost centre. Handle cross-border employment matters with the US team, including A1 certificates and posted-worker filings. Tax and Statutory Compliance File UVA, Zusammenfassende Meldung, and Intrastat via FinanzOnline. Apply reverse-charge and intra-community treatment to cross-border purchases across Austria, Germany, Spain, and the US. Coordinate Körperschaftsteuer returns and advance payments with external advisors. Maintain intercompany and transfer pricing documentation for cost-plus service arrangements. Prepare the annual Forschungsprämie claim, including the FFG Jahresgutachten and supporting cost documentation. Own the statutory filing calendar. Purchasing and Procurement Run procure-to-pay in NetSuite: requisitions, purchase orders, blanket POs, receipts, and three-way match. Act as first-line reviewer for Austrian requisitions, purchase orders, and vendor bills under the purchasing policy and approval authority matrix. Onboard and maintain vendor master data: UID validation, bank verification, tax status, sanctions screening. Manage payment runs, supplier terms, and Austrian cash requirements; feed group treasury forecasting. Track committed and actual spend against budget and grant work packages, including long-lead capital equipment and refractory materials. EU Grant Accounting and Reporting Own financial administration for EU and national grant-funded projects, including Horizon Europe. Track grant cost by work package and eligible cost category: personnel, equipment, subcontracting, other direct costs, indirect flat rate. Prepare periodic cost claims and Financial Statements in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal; ensure personnel-cost methodology, timesheets, and depreciation comply with the Model Grant Agreement. Manage Certificates on the Financial Statements where thresholds are triggered. Act as financial contact for funding bodies and consortium partners, including FFG and aws. Keep grant documentation audit-ready and support grant audits. Systems and Process Operate NetSuite as system of record (multi-subsidiary, multi-currency, multi-book): saved searches, reports, approval workflows, SuiteProcurement. Build, document, and automate Austrian finance process with the Director of Finance & Accounting. Required Qualifications Bilanzbuchhalter under the BiBuG, or equivalent qualification in accounting, finance, or controlling (HAK/HLW, FH, university). Five or more years of full-cycle accounting in Austria, including sole responsibility for a legal entity’s books and the Jahresabschluss under UGB. Working command of Austrian payroll and payroll tax. Practical command of Austrian and EU VAT: intra-community supplies, acquisitions, reverse charge. Professional fluency in German and English. Advanced Excel; ERP-native rather than spreadsheet-dependent. Authorisation to work in Austria. Preferred Qualifications EU grant financial reporting (Horizon Europe or Horizon 2020, EU Innovation Fund, FFG or aws programmes), including periodic cost claims and grant audit experience. US GAAP and reporting into a US parent company. Manufacturing or capital-equipment environment: inventory, work orders, WIP. Personalverrechner certification. Startup or scale-up experience, ideally hardware. Physical Demands Sitting and standing: Extended periods at a desk performing computer-based design, simulation, and documentation work, balanced with time at a lab bench or in the shop during hardware build and testing Lifting and carrying : Lift and carry equipment, test fixtures, or hardware assemblies up to 50 lbs.; heavier items handled with mechanical assistance or team lift Hand dexterity: Frequent use of hands for assembly, fabrication, instrumentation hookup, and operation of test and shop equipment Visual acuity: Ability to read engineering drawings, inspect hardware, and identify dimensional and surface quality features during fabrication and testing PPE compliance: Ability to wear and work effectively in required personal protective equipment, including safety glasses, heat-resistant gloves, safety shoes, and other appropriate gear in high-temperature lab and shop environments Safety acumen: Demonstrated understanding of lab and shop safety protocols, including hazard recognition and risk mitigation in environments involving high-temperature equipment, energized systems, and fabrication machinery Travel: Occasional travel (estimated <5%) for tool or material pickup Working at Tempo Tempo is a lean organization working on exciting challenges, and the people who thrive here share a few things in common beyond their technical skills. Clear, direct communication: You professionally say what you mean, lead with empathy, use tact, ask when you're unsure, and keep the people around you informed without being asked. At a company our size, communication gaps are expensive, and good communicators add to success and efficiency! Low-ego helpfulness: You're willing to jump in on work that isn't strictly yours, whether that's helping a teammate debug something, lending a hand in the shop, or flagging an issue you noticed outside your lane. No one here succeeds in a silo. Intellectual curiosity: You're genuinely interested in how things work, not just your piece of it, but the broader system. Tempo sits at the intersection of chemistry, mechanical engineering, power electronics, and software; the more you understand about the whole, the more valuable you become. jobs.description: About Tempo Based in San Diego, California, Tempo develops thermochemical energy storage (TCES) systems designed for energy-intensive industries. For more information, visit www.tempoenergy.com .   Tempo is seeking a highly skilled and safety-conscious Electronics Technician to join our team. In this role, you will be responsible for the assembly, testing, troubleshooting, and maintenance of complex electronic systems, with a specialized focus on high power and high voltage equipment. You will work closely with our engineering team to ensure the reliability and safety of high-voltage components, power supplies, inverters, and related industrial control systems. Key Responsibilities System Testing & Calibration: Perform routine and complex testing, calibration, and validation of high power electronic systems and high voltage circuitry. Troubleshooting & Repair: Diagnose malfunctions down to the component level in power electronics, switchgear, transformers, motor drives, and energy storage systems. Assembly & Installation: Read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, and mechanical blueprints to assemble and install high voltage panels and subsystems. Safety Compliance: Strictly adhere to all electrical safety protocols, including Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) procedures, arc flash safety, and NFPA 70E standards. Maintenance: Execute preventative and corrective maintenance on high voltage test fixtures and production equipment to minimize downtime. Documentation: Maintain accurate logs of testing data, repair histories, and equipment performance metrics. Draft technical reports summarizing failure analysis. Collaboration: Work alongside electrical and mechanical engineers to prototype new power systems, suggesting design improvements based on field testing. Qualifications Required: Associate Degree in Electronics Engineering Technology, Electrical Engineering Technology, or equivalent military technical training (e.g., Navy Nuclear, Avionics). Minimum of 3–5 years of hands-on experience in electronics manufacturing, testing, or maintenance, with at least 2 years specifically working with high power (>10kW) or high voltage (>600V) systems. Proficiency in using advanced electrical test equipment, including oscilloscopes, multimeters, megohmmeters (meggers), hi-pot testers, and power analyzers. Strong understanding of power conversion topologies (AC/DC, DC/DC, DC/AC). Ability to solder to IPC-J-STD-001 or IPC-A-610 standards. Demonstrated knowledge of high voltage safety practices, OSHA electrical safety standards, and proper use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Maintain a professional, organized, and welcoming reception area while directing guests to the appropriate host. Assist with accurate and timely processing of expense reports and maintaining digital filing systems. jobs.title: Financial Planning & Analysis Intern
jobs.description: About Tempo Based in San Diego, California, Tempo develops thermochemical energy storage (TCES) systems designed for energy-intensive industries. The platform enables industrial operators to shift energy use over time by sourcing power when it is most cost-effective and enables the electrification of high-temperature industrial heat at a cost advantage to using fossil fuels. By storing electricity thermochemically, the system delivers a continuous stream of combustion-free, high-temperature air at up to 1,200°C. Tempo is backed by leading climate and energy investors, including Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Khosla Ventures, and Prelude Ventures. For more information, visit www.tempoenergy.com . Tempo is hiring a part-time FP&A Intern to work alongside the finance team during the academic year. This is a build role. Several things the company currently needs — the pricing models behind customer RFP responses, the unit-economics model covering Section 45X credits and cost of goods sold, and the recurring reporting package for management and investors — need to become standing, documented processes. You will help build them and then run them. You will also support the 2027 budgeting cycle end to end. The work is visible. Pricing models inform numbers Tempo quotes to customers, and the reporting package goes to our management team and our investors. Expect real ownership, real deadlines, and close review. About Tempo Tempo develops thermochemical energy storage for industrial heat and power. Our Thermochemical Energy Storage (TCES) System charges on low-cost electricity using self-resistive charging, stores that energy in Thermochemical Storage Material (TSM) inside a containerized Thermal Module, and discharges continuous high-temperature air to the customer's process. Systems are deployed as a Thermal Array of modules with their associated Power Cabinets.  What You Will Work On RFP and project pricing models Build and maintain the model used to price Thermal Array configurations in customer RFPs and proposals — capital cost, installation, operations and maintenance, contract term, and delivered cost of energy. Run scenario and sensitivity analysis across system configuration, site conditions, electricity pricing, and financing assumptions. Translate model output into the pricing exhibits, summary tables, and assumption schedules that go into RFP responses. Maintain a versioned assumption library so pricing is consistent and auditable across bids. Section 45X and cost of goods sold Build the unit-level cost model for the Thermal Module and Power Cabinet — bill of materials, vendor quotes, labor, freight, and overhead absorption. Model Section 45X Advanced Manufacturing Production Credit eligibility and value per unit, including timing of recognition and the effect on gross margin and cash flow. Track standard versus actual cost as production data comes in, and explain the variances. Maintain the cost-down curve that underpins long-term margin projections, and keep it tied to procurement and engineering inputs. Management and investor reporting Build the monthly reporting package: profit and loss against budget, cash and runway, headcount, and operating KPIs, with written variance commentary. Establish the reporting calendar and source-data workflow so the package is produced on a predictable cadence instead of assembled from scratch each period. Prepare the recurring metrics and exhibits used in investor updates and board materials. Document the process so the reporting structure survives handoff. 2027 budgeting process Support the 2027 annual budget end to end — build and distribute the department templates, collect and stress-test submissions from functional leads, and consolidate them into a single company plan. Build the driver-based operating model behind the budget: headcount and compensation, production volume and unit cost, capital spending, and operating expense by department. Roll the budget into the monthly reporting package so budget-versus-actual reporting starts on day one of the fiscal year rather than months into it. Maintain the budget calendar, track open items across departments, and keep a clean record of assumptions and approved changes through reforecast cycles. What We Are Looking For Required Currently enrolled undergraduate in finance, accounting, economics, engineering, or a related field, with at least two semesters of relevant coursework completed. Strong Excel. You should be comfortable building a model from a blank sheet, not only editing someone else's, and familiar with three-statement mechanics. Precision with numbers and the habit of checking your own work before it goes anywhere. Availability of 15–20 hours per week during the academic term on a consistent weekly schedule. Clear written communication — you will write commentary that management and investors read. Working familiarity with AI tools such as Claude or ChatGPT, and the judgment to use them well — we expect you to lean on them to build model structure, clean and reconcile data, write formulas, and draft commentary, and we expect you to check every number that comes out before it lands in a model or a report. Helpful, not required Coursework or prior exposure to manufacturing or cost accounting. Familiarity with Inflation Reduction Act tax credits (45X, 48E, 45Y) or project finance. Experience with NetSuite, QuickBooks, or a comparable ERP. Interest in energy storage, industrial decarbonization, or hardware businesses. What You Will Get Out of It Ownership of models and reporting structures that stay in use after the internship ends. A working understanding of how a hardware company prices, costs, and reports itself — including tax credit mechanics that most finance students never see. A full annual planning cycle from the inside — template to submission to consolidated plan to budget-versus-actual reporting. Direct mentorship from Tempo's finance leadership, with regular feedback. Consideration for extension or a full-time offer for strong performers.   Compensation Range  The US base hourly range for this part-time position is $25.00-$35.00 an hour. Our hourly ranges are determined by role, level, and location. Within the range, individual pay is determined by additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, location, and relevant education or training.    Physical Demands Sitting and standing: Extended periods at a desk performing computer-based design, simulation, and documentation work, balanced with time at a lab bench or in the shop during hardware build and testing Lifting and carrying : Lift and carry equipment, test fixtures, or hardware assemblies up to 50 lbs.; heavier items handled with mechanical assistance or team lift Hand dexterity: Frequent use of hands for assembly, fabrication, instrumentation hookup, and operation of test and shop equipment Visual acuity: Ability to read engineering drawings, inspect hardware, and identify dimensional and surface quality features during fabrication and testing PPE compliance: Ability to wear and work effectively in required personal protective equipment, including safety glasses, heat-resistant gloves, safety shoes, and other appropriate gear in high-temperature lab and shop environments Safety acumen: Demonstrated understanding of lab and shop safety protocols, including hazard recognition and risk mitigation in environments involving high-temperature equipment, energized systems, and fabrication machinery Travel: Occasional travel (estimated <5%) for tool or material pickup Working at Tempo Tempo is a lean organization working on exciting challenges, and the people who thrive here share a few things in common beyond their technical skills. Clear, direct communication: You professionally say what you mean, lead with empathy, use tact, ask when you're unsure, and keep the people around you informed without being asked. At a company our size, communication gaps are expensive, and good communicators add to success and efficiency! Low-ego helpfulness: You're willing to jump in on work that isn't strictly yours, whether that's helping a teammate debug something, lending a hand in the shop, or flagging an issue you noticed outside your lane. No one here succeeds in a silo. Intellectual curiosity: You're genuinely interested in how things work, not just your piece of it, but the broader system. Tempo sits at the intersection of chemistry, mechanical engineering, power electronics, and software; the more you understand about the whole, the more valuable you become.
